scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “Perfect completeness for 2-to-1 games” (preprints/Perfect-completeness-for-2-to-1-games-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 105 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2691ba6bd2ac7159), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 1. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every fixed rational δ ∈ (0, 1) there are an integer q = q(δ) ≥ 2 and a deterministic polynomial-time reduction from 3-SAT to 2-to-1 games with alphabets [2q] and [q] such that: (i) a satisfiable formula produces a game of value 1; (ii) an unsatisfiable formula produces a game of value at most δ. The output contains a nonempty explicit list of unweighted edge occurrences and an explicit table for every projection map. Every table has exactly two preimages for each right answer. The polynomial running-time bound is in the ordinary binary input length; its degree and constants may depend on the fixed δ.
